independent_derivation: Specialize the frozen family grammar to r=2 and arbitrary q>=1.
Parent edges give each a_i adjacency only to s and z among the fixed/variable classes; each b_j is adjacent to t,m,z; there are no A-B or B-B edges.
Use the frozen proper extension restriction s=1,t=2,m=2,z=1,a1=3,a2=4 and independently choose every b_j in {3,4}.
For each b_j, both 3 and 4 differ from all its neighbors' fixed colors 2,2,1; because B is stable, choices are independent. Hence X(q)=2^q.
Add a1,a2 to the seed. Since z is adjacent to both selected vertices, z acquires seeded neighbors and is no longer in Y0.
The parent grammar has no second Y0 vertex in the post-constructor G_{2,q} state, so residual Y0 is empty.
The graph, exact lists, partition and proof-relevant Y0 incidence are independent of the chosen B extension colors; therefore one canonical proof-interface SIGMA occurs at each fixed q.
Retaining q itself as multiplicity metadata yields one distinct size-catalog record for every q, hence exactly N records over 1<=q<=N.
